results.content: Key recommendations include developing culturally responsive Digital Learning environments, integrating traditional practices like ‘chavruta’ into digital platforms, and investing in flexible technological infrastructure to support diverse pedagogical approaches within the unique Israeli educational context. digital learning; higher education; lecturers’ perceptions; pedagogical innovation; technological integration; Israeli education; cultural adaptation; educational challenges. By focusing on lecturers’ perspectives, it provides unique insights into the practical challenges and opportunities associated with implementing Digital Learning, which is essential for developing effective policies and support systems in higher education institutions. * Cultural adaptation of Digital Learning: The innovative approaches developed by lecturers in response to challenges such as infrastructural disparities, multicultural student bodies, and the integration of military experiences into education, demonstrate how Digital Learning can be adapted to specific cultural contexts. Firstly, by examining the implementation of Digital Learning in the culturally diverse context of Israeli higher education, our research provides valuable insights into how cultural factors shape the adoption and effectiveness of educational technologies.

results.title: Virtual reality in education: global trends, challenges, and impacts ...
results.content: Building on these pedagogical foundations, virtual reality (VR) has been increasingly integrated into educational settings since the early 2010s, enabling innovative applications such as the simulation of scientific experiments, practical skills training in fields like medicine and engineering, and the creation of immersive environments for distance learning [57:1171–82. A total of 41 articles were published in journals indexed by the Emerging Sources Citation Index (ESCI), reflecting increasing scholarly interest in the application of virtual reality (VR) in education within emerging or developing academic outlets. *Interactive Learning Environments* and the *International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education* contributed six articles (6.19%), with a substantial total of 119 and 104 citations, respectively, showing that VR research in interactive learning and higher education also garners significant attention. This study contributes to the growing body of literature on immersive technologies by offering a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of virtual reality (VR) applications in education.
